issue.body:
This is an effort to provide the correct `#[reflect_value(...)]` attributes where they are needed.  

Supersedes #1533 and resolves #1528.

---

I am working under the following assumptions (thanks to @bjorn3 and @Davier for advice here):

- Any `enum` that derives `Reflect` and one or more of { `Serialize`, `Deserialize`, `PartialEq`, `Hash` } needs a `#[reflect_value(...)]` attribute containing the same subset of { `Serialize`, `Deserialize`, `PartialEq`, `Hash` } that is present on the derive.
- Same as above for `struct` and `#[reflect(...)]`, respectively.
- If a `struct` is used as a component, it should also have `#[reflect(Component)]`
- All reflected types should be registered in their plugins

I treated the following as components (added `#[reflect(Component)]` if necessary):
- `bevy_render`
  - `struct RenderLayers`
- `bevy_transform`
  - `struct GlobalTransform`
  - `struct Parent`
  - `struct Transform`
- `bevy_ui`
  - `struct Style`

Not treated as components:
- `bevy_math`
  - `struct Size<T>`
  - `struct Rect<T>`
  - Note: The updates for `Size<T>` and `Rect<T>` in `bevy::math::geometry` required using @Davier's suggestion to add `+ PartialEq` to the trait bound. I then registered the specific types used over in `bevy_ui` such as `Size<Val>`, etc. in `bevy_ui`'s plugin, since `bevy::math` does not contain a plugin.
- `bevy_render`
  - `struct Color`
  - `struct PipelineSpecialization`
  - `struct ShaderSpecialization`
  - `enum PrimitiveTopology`
  - `enum IndexFormat`

Not Addressed:
- I am not searching for components in Bevy that are _not_ reflected. So if there are components that are not reflected that should be reflected, that will need to be figured out in another PR.
- I only added `#[reflect(...)]` or `#[reflect_value(...)]` entries for the set of four traits { `Serialize`, `Deserialize`, `PartialEq`, `Hash` } _if they were derived via `#[derive(...)]`_. I did not look for manual trait implementations of the same set of four, nor did I consider any traits outside the four.  Are those other possibilities something that needs to be looked into?

body:
Hey, this has indeed solved the issue of saving the scene. But now if I try to load the same scene back into the game I receive the following error.

`Feb 28 22:54:16.854  WARN bevy_asset::asset_server: encountered an error while loading an asset: No registration found for std::collections::hash::set::HashSet<alloc::string::String, ahash::random_state::RandomState>`

Hmm. From a glance that appears to be different sort of problem, but I am not very familiar with the asset system. Just in case, would you mind testing with #1536 and see if the more comprehensive reflection cleanup work I did happened to help?

> Hey, this has indeed solved the issue of saving the scene. But now if I try to load the same scene back into the game I receive the following error.
> 
> `Feb 28 22:54:16.854 WARN bevy_asset::asset_server: encountered an error while loading an asset: No registration found for std::collections::hash::set::HashSet<alloc::string::String, ahash::random_state::RandomState>`

You have to register the types of your components in your app builder for them to be usable in a scene.
For example, a lot of basic types are registered in `bevy_reflect`: https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/3319195f9036e9ee301545632b98f1090a3ba3b0/crates/bevy_reflect/src/impls/bevy_app.rs#L11-L15
Types used for render are registered in `bevy_render` https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/89a41bc62843be5f92b4b978f6d801af4de14a2d/crates/bevy_render/src/lib.rs#L129-L134
and so on...

Is this from only default components of Bevy, or are you adding a custom component that is using a `HashSet`?

As part of #1536 I have started going through the default components in Bevy that derive`Reflect` and making sure they are registered. I've already found a one that was not being registered.  **Edit:** #1536 is ready to test out...or at least I've addressed all the problems found so far.

@CleanCut what do you think about adding in your PR #1536  to [`bevy_render`](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/main/crates/bevy_render/src/lib.rs) (only place it's used in a public component I think) or [`bevy_core`](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/main/crates/bevy_core/src/lib.rs) (it's a core type after all)
```rust
.register_type::<bevy_utils::HashSet<String>>()
```
after a quick search it seems it's the only `HashSet` used in something public, no other `HashSet<T>`

There's also a `HashMap` in `bevy_sprite` that would probably error when loading a scene with a `TextureAtlas`: https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/main/crates/bevy_sprite/src/texture_atlas.rs#L25
oh right, my bad, the texture atlas itself is a ressource, so probably not serialised in a scene
The manual `Reflect` implementations for `Vec`, `Hashmap` and `Cow` are in `bevy_reflect/src/impl/std.rs`, and they should be implementing `GetTypeRegistration` too

> The manual `Reflect` implementations for `Vec`, `Hashmap` and `Cow` are in `bevy_reflect/src/impl/std.rs`, and they should be implementing `GetTypeRegistration` too

This feels like a good place to start a new PR. Can you check out this PR on my fork and let me know if I'm heading in the right direction? https://github.com/CleanCut/bevy/pull/2
